First, we take the Laplace transform of both sides of the differential equation. Using the linearity property, we have

$$
L{{y}^{′}}+3L{y}=L{\operatorname{sin}⁡2t}+L{\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}.
$$

Using the formula for the transform of a derivative $L{{y}^{′}}=sY(s)-y(0)$ and the standard trigonometric transforms

$$
L{\operatorname{sin}⁡2t}=\frac{2}{{s}^{2}+4},\,L{\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+4},
$$

we substitute the known values. Note that $y(0)=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(sY(s)-1)+3Y(s) & =\frac{2}{{s}^{2}+4}+\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+4} \\ (s+3)Y(s)-1 & =\frac{s+2}{{s}^{2}+4}\end{aligned}
$$

We rearrange to solve for $Y(s).$ First, add $1$ to the right-hand side and find a common denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}(s+3)Y(s) & =1+\frac{s+2}{{s}^{2}+4} \\ (s+3)Y(s) & =\frac{{s}^{2}+4}{{s}^{2}+4}+\frac{s+2}{{s}^{2}+4} \\ (s+3)Y(s) & =\frac{{s}^{2}+s+6}{{s}^{2}+4}\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing by $(s+3),$ we obtain

$$
Y(s)=\frac{{s}^{2}+s+6}{(s+3)({s}^{2}+4)}.
$$

Next, we perform a partial fraction decomposition. Since the denominator has a linear factor $(s+3)$ and an irreducible quadratic factor $({s}^{2}+4),$ we write

$$
\frac{{s}^{2}+s+6}{(s+3)({s}^{2}+4)}=\frac{A}{s+3}+\frac{Bs+C}{{s}^{2}+4}.
$$

To find the constants, we clear the denominators:

$$
{s}^{2}+s+6=A({s}^{2}+4)+(Bs+C)(s+3)
$$

- Setting $s=-3,$ we have
 

$$
(-3)^{2}+(-3)+6=A((-3)^{2}+4)+0\,⟹\,12=13A\,⟹\,A=\frac{12}{13}.
$$

- Comparing the coefficients of ${s}^{2},$ we have
  

$$
1=A+B\,⟹\,1=\frac{12}{13}+B\,⟹\,B=\frac{1}{13}.
$$

- Comparing the constant terms, we have
 

$$
6=4A+3C\,⟹\,6=4(\frac{12}{13})+3C\,⟹\,C=\frac{10}{13}.
$$

Thus, the decomposition is

$$
Y(s)=\frac{(\frac{12}{13})}{13(s+3)}+\frac{(\frac{1}{13}s+\frac{10}{13})}{{s}^{2}+4}=\frac{12}{13(s+3)}+\frac{s+10}{13({s}^{2}+4)}.
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s+3}} & ={e}^{-3t} \\ {L}^{-1}{\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+4}} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡2t \\ {L}^{-1}{\frac{2}{{s}^{2}+4}} & =\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, taking the inverse Laplace transform of $Y(s),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y(t) & =\frac{12}{13}{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s+3}}+\frac{1}{13}{L}^{-1}{\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+4}}+\frac{5}{13}{L}^{-1}{\frac{2}{{s}^{2}+4}} \\ y(t) & =\frac{12}{13}{e}^{-3t}+\frac{5}{13}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t+\frac{1}{13}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t.\end{aligned}
$$

  • Setting s=−3, we have (−3)2+(−3)+6=A((−3)2+4)+0⟹12=13A⟹A=1213.

  • Comparing the constant terms, we have 6=4A+3C⟹6=4(1213)+3C⟹C=1013.

Thus, the decomposition is Y(s)=(1213)13(s+3)+(113s+1013)s2+4=1213(s+3)+s+1013(s2+4).
